questions.description: You have k lists of sorted integers in non-decreasing order. Find the smallest range that includes at least one number from each of the k lists.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the smallest range containing at least one element from each of K sorted lists?
questions.hint: Insert the first element of each list into a Min-Heap while tracking the current maximum. Pop the minimum, evaluate the current range, and advance in that list.
commonMistakes: Stopping traversal when one list ends without realizing no further valid range can contain elements from all K lists
Not properly tracking the global maximum while extracting elements from the Min-Heap
followUpQuestions: Can this be solved using a Sliding Window on a single merged list of all elements?
What if ties in range size occur and require returning the range with the smallest start value?

questions.name: Meeting Rooms III
questions.description: You are given an integer n representing available rooms numbered 0 to n - 1 and a 2D array of meetings. Allocate rooms prioritizing lowest room index and find the room that held the most meetings.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you track room availability and meeting delays using two Min-Heaps?
questions.hint: Maintain two Min-Heaps: one for available room indices and one for busy rooms ordered by end time.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to sort meetings by start time before processing
Failing to tie-break room selection by lowest room index when multiple rooms are free
followUpQuestions: How would you return all rooms tied for hosting the maximum number of meetings?
How would you handle room priority if meeting durations vary continuously?
questions.timeComplexity: O(m log m + m log n)

questions.name: Number of Islands
questions.description: Given an m x n 2D binary grid grid which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you count connected components in a 2D grid matrix using DFS or BFS?
questions.hint: Traverse every cell in the grid. When encountering '1', increment island count and use DFS/BFS to sink or mark all adjacent connected '1's as '0'.
commonMistakes: Forgetting out-of-bounds boundary checks before accessing grid elements
Stack overflow exceptions on large grids when using recursive DFS without optimizing visited state
followUpQuestions: How would you solve this using Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union)?
What if the grid is too large to fit into memory?

questions.name: Clone Graph
questions.description: Given a reference of a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy (clone) of the graph.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you create a deep copy of an undirected graph with arbitrary cycle references?
questions.hint: Use a Hash Map to track mapped pairs between original nodes and cloned nodes during DFS/BFS traversal to prevent infinite cycles.
commonMistakes: Performing a shallow copy instead of cloning individual neighbor references
Getting stuck in an infinite recursion loop due to cyclic references in undirected edges
followUpQuestions: How does the BFS implementation compare in memory efficiency with the recursive DFS approach?
How would you clone a directed graph with weighted edges?

questions.name: Flood Fill
questions.description: An image is represented by an m x n integer grid image. Perform a flood fill on the image starting from the pixel image[sr][sc].
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you implement the paint bucket tool functionality on an image grid using graph traversal?
questions.hint: Traverse 4-directionally from start cell using DFS/BFS, replacing starting color with new color. Short-circuit if target color matches starting color.
commonMistakes: Infinite recursion loop when initial color matches the target replacement color
Missing diagonal checks when 4-directional adjacency is required
followUpQuestions: How would you adapt this if 8-directional filling was required?
Can this be written iteratively using an explicit Stack?

questions.name: Rotting Oranges
questions.description: You are given an m x n grid where each cell can represent empty, fresh orange, or rotten orange. Return the minimum number of minutes that must elapse until no cell has a fresh orange.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you simulate multi-source simultaneous propagation in a grid using BFS?
questions.hint: Add all initially rotten oranges to a Queue at once. Use Multi-Source Breadth-First Search level-by-level to rot adjacent fresh oranges.
commonMistakes: Using DFS instead of BFS, which fails to simulate simultaneous time progression across sources
Incrementing time steps when no new oranges were rotted in a level pass
followUpQuestions: How do you quickly detect if fresh oranges remain isolated from all rotten oranges?
What is the maximum possible time units needed to rot an m x n grid?

questions.name: Course Schedule
questions.description: There are a total of numCourses courses you have to take, labeled from 0 to numCourses - 1. Return true if you can finish all courses given prerequisite pairs.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you detect cycles in a directed graph representing prerequisite constraints?
questions.hint: Model prerequisites as directed edges. Use Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm with in-degrees) or DFS with states (unvisited, visiting, visited).
commonMistakes: Assuming the graph is connected or undirected
Using simple visited boolean set without tracking current DFS recursion path stack states
followUpQuestions: How does Kahn's BFS Algorithm detect cycles compared to DFS color-marking?
What if there are multiple disconnected course components?

questions.name: Course Schedule II
questions.description: Return the ordering of courses you should take to finish all courses. If it is impossible to finish all courses, return an empty array.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you generate a valid linear ordering of tasks with prerequisite dependencies?
questions.hint: Perform Kahn's Algorithm (BFS topological sort) using in-degree counts. Append processed nodes to ordering list.
commonMistakes: Returning partial topological ordering when a cycle is present
Constructing graph edges in reversed direction (prerequisites -> course vs course -> prerequisites)
followUpQuestions: How would you return all possible valid course ordering paths?
How do you handle parallel processing of courses with independent prerequisites?

questions.name: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
questions.description: Find all grid coordinates from which water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you optimize multi-ocean water flow analysis by traversing backwards from ocean boundaries?
questions.hint: Perform DFS/BFS from Pacific ocean borders going uphill (`heights[next] >= heights[curr]`), repeat for Atlantic borders, and take set intersection.

Checking strict inequality instead of non-decreasing height conditions
followUpQuestions: What is the advantage of reverse traversal over forward simulation?
How would you handle dynamic terrain height adjustments?

questions.name: Surrounded Regions
questions.description: Given an m x n matrix board containing 'X' and 'O', capture all regions that are 4-directionally surrounded by 'X'.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you capture enclosed regions in a grid without accidentally overwriting boundary-connected regions?
questions.hint: Traverse boundary cells containing 'O' and use DFS to mark connected 'O's as safe/temp ('#'). Flip all remaining 'O's to 'X' and safe ones back.
commonMistakes: Starting traversal from internal cells instead of outer boundary edges
Forgetting to restore temporary boundary-connected markers back to original values
followUpQuestions: Can this be implemented using Union-Find by connecting edge 'O's to a dummy node?
What is the maximum depth of recursion stack for an m x n matrix?

questions.name: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
questions.description: Given n nodes and an array of undirected edges, return the number of connected components in the graph.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you count connected components in an undirected graph using Disjoint Set Union (DSU)?
questions.hint: Initialize N components. Loop through edges; perform Union operations on connected nodes and decrement component count when distinct sets merge.

Incorrect parent array initialization
followUpQuestions: How does the time complexity of Union-Find compare with DFS component counting?
How would you handle dynamic edge additions over time?

questions.name: Graph Valid Tree
questions.description: Given n nodes labeled from 0 to n - 1 and a list of undirected edges, check whether these edges form a valid tree.
questions.interviewQuestion: What conditions must an undirected graph satisfy to be considered a valid tree?
questions.hint: A graph is a valid tree if and only if it has exactly `n - 1` edges and all `n` nodes are fully connected without cycles.
commonMistakes: Checking only for cycle absence while ignoring disconnected components
Not short-circuiting when `edges.length != n - 1`
followUpQuestions: How do tree validation conditions differ between directed and undirected graphs?
Can you validate this graph using pure Breadth-First Search?

questions.name: Redundant Connection
questions.description: Return an edge that can be removed so that the resulting graph is a tree of n nodes.

questions.hint: Iterate through edges one by one. If both endpoints already share the same parent root in DSU, this edge creates a cycle and is redundant.

Modifying the original graph adjacency list while performing Union-Find operations
followUpQuestions: How would you solve Redundant Connection II for directed graphs?
Can this be solved using DFS cycle detection?

questions.name: Word Ladder
questions.description: Given two words, beginWord and endWord, and a dictionary wordList, return the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence.

followUpQuestions: How can Bidirectional BFS optimize search space for Word Ladder?
How would you reconstruct and print all shortest transformation paths (Word Ladder II)?

questions.name: Open the Lock
questions.description: You have a lock with 4 circular wheels. Given deadends and target, return the minimum total number of turns required to reach target.

Incorrectly wrapping wheel rotation modulo math (0 -> 9 or 9 -> 0)

How would you adapt the algorithm if wheels had variable numbers of digits?

questions.name: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix

questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the shortest path in an 8-directionally connected grid matrix?
questions.hint: Perform BFS starting at (0, 0), moving across valid 8-directional neighbors with value 0, tracking layer/distance steps.

Checking only 4 directions instead of required 8 directions
followUpQuestions: Can this shortest path search be optimized using the A* Search algorithm?
How does grid size impact queue size bounds in memory?

questions.name: All Paths From Source to Target
questions.description: Given a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of n nodes, find all possible paths from node 0 to node n - 1 and return them in any order.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you enumerate all paths from source to target in a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)?
questions.hint: Use Backtracking / DFS. Maintain a running path vector, append current node, recurse into neighbors, and backtrack after processing.

Forgetting to copy path state before pushing to final result array

What is the maximum number of potential paths in a DAG with N nodes?

questions.name: Keys and Rooms

questions.interviewQuestion: How do you determine if all nodes in a directed graph are reachable starting from node 0?
questions.hint: Traverse graph from room 0 using DFS/BFS, keeping track of visited room numbers in a Set. Check if visited set size equals total rooms.

Assuming keys are symmetric (room A key opens room B implies room B key opens room A)
followUpQuestions: How does this problem reduce to standard component reachability?
What changes if keys can break or have single-use limitations?

questions.name: Is Graph Bipartite?
questions.description: Given an undirected graph, return true if and only if it is bipartite (nodes can be partitioned into two independent sets).
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you verify if a graph can be 2-colored such that no adjacent nodes share the same color?
questions.hint: Use BFS/DFS graph coloring. Assign initial color 0 to an unvisited node, alternate neighbor colors to 1, and check for color conflicts.

Concluding graph is bipartite without checking every edge transition
followUpQuestions: What is the relationship between odd-length cycles and bipartite graphs?
How can this be solved using Union-Find?

questions.name: Reorder Routes to Make All Paths Lead to the City Zero

questions.hint: Build an undirected adjacency list marking original forward edges as weight 1 and artificial reverse edges as weight 0. Traversal from 0 counts necessary reversals.

Confusing original edge orientations with reversed virtual helper edges
followUpQuestions: Why is a tree structure guaranteed by the problem constraints here?
Can this be solved using topological sort logic?

questions.name: Minimum Height Trees
questions.description: Find all roots of trees that have the minimum possible height among all possible choices of root.

Trimming inner non-leaf nodes prematurely
followUpQuestions: Why can there be at most two centroid roots in any valid tree?
How does finding tree centroids relate to tree diameter?

questions.name: Network Delay Time
questions.description: Given times as directed weighted edges and a starting node k, return the minimum time for all n nodes to receive the signal.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the single-source shortest path to all nodes in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights?

Not skipping stale heap entries whose recorded distance exceeds current computed array distance

What is the time complexity of Dijkstra using a Fibonacci Heap?

questions.name: Valid Palindrome
questions.description: Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome, considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring cases.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you verify if a string is a palindrome while skipping non-alphanumeric characters in-place?

Creating new filtered strings in memory instead of evaluating in-place with O(1) space

What if you are allowed to remove at most one character to make it a palindrome (Valid Palindrome II)?

questions.name: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

questions.name: 3Sum
questions.description: Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.

questions.name: 4Sum

followUpQuestions: How would you structure a recursive function to solve general K-Sum?
What early-pruning optimizations can be applied based on min/max possible sums?

questions.name: Container With Most Water

How does this problem differ from Trapping Rain Water?

questions.name: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
questions.description: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, remove the duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once. Return the number of unique elements.

followUpQuestions: What if duplicates are allowed to appear at most twice (Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II)?
How would you adapt this for unsorted arrays without using extra space?

questions.name: Squares of a Sorted Array
questions.description: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array of the squares of each number sorted in non-decreasing order.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you construct a sorted array of squared values from a sorted array containing negative numbers in O(n) time?

Filling the result array from front to back without tracking pointer indices correctly

questions.name: Sort Colors

questions.interviewQuestion: How do you sort an array consisting only of 0s, 1s, and 2s in a single pass with O(1) space?
questions.hint: Use the Dutch National Flag algorithm: low pointer for 0s, mid pointer for 1s, and high pointer for 2s.
commonMistakes: Advancing the mid pointer after swapping with high without checking the swapped element
Using two passes (counting sort) when a single pass is requested
followUpQuestions: How would you extend this algorithm to sort k distinct colors in linear time?
Why can't mid advance after swapping with high?

questions.name: Boats to Save People
questions.description: You are given an array people where people[i] is the weight of the ith person, and an infinite number of boats where each boat can carry at most limit weight and at most two people. Return the minimum number of boats to carry every person.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you pair heavy and light people to minimize the total number of rescue boats required?
questions.hint: Sort weights. Pair the heaviest remaining person (right pointer) with the lightest (left pointer) if their sum is within limit; otherwise, give the heavy person their own boat.
commonMistakes: Forgetting that a boat can carry at most TWO people, regardless of remaining capacity
Not handling the edge case where the left and right pointers meet on the same person
followUpQuestions: What if boats could carry an unlimited number of people as long as the total weight limit is met?
Can this be solved without sorting if person weights are bounded in a small range?

questions.name: Move Zeroes
questions.description: Given an integer array nums, move all 0's to the end of it while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you shift all zeroes to the end of an array in-place without altering the order of non-zero elements?
questions.hint: Use a pointer to track the position of the next non-zero element. Iterate through the array and swap non-zero elements to this position.
commonMistakes: Copying elements to a secondary array, violating the in-place constraint
Performing unnecessary self-swaps when no zeroes have been encountered yet
followUpQuestions: How can you minimize the total number of write/swap operations when the array contains mostly zeroes?
How does this relate to the Remove Element problem?

questions.name: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the longest contiguous substring containing all unique characters in O(n) time?
questions.hint: Use a sliding window with a Hash Set or Hash Map to track unique characters. Shrink window from the left whenever a duplicate is found.
commonMistakes: Moving the left pointer to map.get(char) without checking if it is already behind the current left index
Not resetting/shrinking character states correctly on duplicates
followUpQuestions: Can you optimize window shrinking using last seen character index positions?
How does space complexity change if the character set includes arbitrary Unicode values?

questions.name: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
questions.description: You are given a string s and an integer k. You can choose any character of the string and change it to any other uppercase English character at most k times. Return the length of the longest substring containing the same letter.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the maximum length substring of identical characters obtainable by making at most K replacements?
questions.hint: Maintain character frequencies in a window. A window is valid if (window_length - max_frequency) <= k.
questions.pattern: Sliding Window with Max Frequency Tracking
commonMistakes: Decrementing maxFreq when shrinking the left window bound (it only needs to update when finding a new maximum)
Recalculating frequency maps from scratch at each step
followUpQuestions: Why is it safe to keep maxFreq stale while sliding the window?
How would this problem change if replacing costs differed between characters?

questions.name: Permutation in String
questions.description: Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1, or false otherwise.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you check if a target string contains any permutation of a given pattern substring?
questions.hint: Maintain a fixed-size sliding window equal to s1.length and compare window character frequencies with s1's frequencies.
commonMistakes: Comparing entire frequency arrays in O(26) on every step instead of tracking a running count of matching characters
Not handling cases where s1 is longer than s2
followUpQuestions: How can you optimize match validation using a matches count variable to check in O(1) time?
How does this relate to the Find All Anagrams problem?

questions.name: Minimum Window Substring
questions.description: Given two strings s and t of lengths m and n respectively, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included in the window.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the smallest contiguous substring that contains all characters of a target string?
questions.hint: Expand right to meet required target character counts, then contract left to minimize length while target requirements stay satisfied.
commonMistakes: Failing to account for character duplicate frequencies present in string t
Incorrectly checking substring equality instead of maintaining running have and need counts
followUpQuestions: How would you optimize search time if string s contains millions of non-target characters?
How do you handle returning empty strings when no valid window exists?

questions.name: Sliding Window Maximum
questions.description: You are given an array of integers nums and a sliding window of size k moving from left to right. Return the max sliding window.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the maximum element in every contiguous sub-array window of size K in O(n) total time?
questions.hint: Store indices in a Monotonic Decreasing Deque. Keep the front as maximum, popping smaller back elements before inserting new items.
commonMistakes: Storing values instead of indices in the deque, making window boundary expulsion checks impossible
Allowing smaller elements to remain in the back of the deque
followUpQuestions: Can this be solved using a Max-Heap or Segment Tree, and what are their time complexities?
How can this be solved using Prefix and Suffix Max arrays?

questions.name: Maximum Average Subarray I
questions.description: You are given an integer array nums consisting of n elements and an integer k. Find the contiguous subarray of length k that has the maximum average value, and return that maximum average. Any answer with a calculation error less than 10^-5 will be accepted.
questions.interviewQuestion: Given an integer array and a fixed window size k, find the contiguous subarray of size k with the highest average. Optimize your solution to run in linear time instead of recalculating the sum for every window.
questions.hint: Instead of computing the sum of every k-length subarray from scratch, calculate the sum of the first window once. Then slide the window by removing the leftmost element and adding the next element. Keep track of the maximum window sum and divide by k at the end.
commonMistakes: Recalculating the sum of every window, resulting in O(n*k) time complexity.
Forgetting to subtract the element leaving the window before adding the new one.
Using integer division instead of floating-point division for the average.
Not initializing the first window sum correctly.
Updating the maximum average instead of the maximum window sum, causing unnecessary floating-point operations.
followUpQuestions: How would you solve this if the window size were variable instead of fixed?
What if you needed to return the starting index of the maximum average subarray?
How would you find the minimum average subarray of size k?
Can this problem be solved in O(1) extra space?
What changes if the array elements arrive as a stream?

questions.name: Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length
questions.description: Given a string s and an integer k, return the maximum number of vowel letters in any substring of s with length k.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the maximum number of vowels in any fixed window of size K?
questions.hint: Count vowels in the initial K window. Slide the window right by adding the new character and subtracting the left character.
commonMistakes: Re-counting vowels for the entire window at each step instead of updating counts in O(1)
Not handling strings shorter than length k
followUpQuestions: How would you optimize character lookup for arbitrary vowel sets?
Can you terminate early if max count reaches k?

questions.name: Fruit Into Baskets
questions.description: You are visiting a farm that has a single row of fruit trees. You have two baskets, and each basket can only hold a single type of fruit. Return the maximum number of fruits you can collect.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the longest contiguous subarray containing at most two distinct elements?
questions.hint: Use a sliding window with a frequency map. Shrink from the left when the map size exceeds 2.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to completely remove keys from the map when their count drops to 0
Confusing total fruit count with distinct fruit types
followUpQuestions: How does this generalize to K baskets instead of 2?
Can this be solved with O(1) space if fruit types are bounded?

questions.name: Subarray Product Less Than K
questions.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the number of contiguous subarrays where the product of all the elements in the subarray is strictly less than k.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you count contiguous subarrays with product strictly less than K in linear time?
questions.hint: Expand right by multiplying. Shrink left by dividing when product >= k. At each valid step, add `right - left + 1` to total count.
commonMistakes: Not handling k <= 1 edge cases (where no positive integer product can be strictly less than k)
Incorrectly incrementing total count by 1 instead of window length (`right - left + 1`)
followUpQuestions: How would you handle negative numbers or zeroes in the array?
What if precision issues arise with large products?

questions.name: Binary Subarrays With Sum
questions.description: Given a binary array nums and an integer goal, return the number of non-empty subarrays with a sum equal to goal.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you count subarrays with an exact sum in a binary array using sliding window?
questions.hint: Compute `atMost(goal) - atMost(goal - 1)` using sliding window, or use Prefix Sum with a Hash Map.
questions.pattern: Sliding Window (At Most K Trick) / Prefix Sum
commonMistakes: Attempting a direct variable-size sliding window without accounting for zeroes expanding valid window boundaries
Forgetting to handle goal = 0 correctly in `atMost(goal - 1)`
followUpQuestions: Why does a standard sliding window fail on exact sum queries when zeroes are present?
How does this compare to Subarray Sum Equals K?

questions.name: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
questions.description: Given an array of positive integers nums and a positive integer target, return the minimal length of a subarray whose sum is greater than or equal to target. If there is no such subarray, return 0.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you find the minimum length contiguous subarray whose sum reaches a target threshold?
questions.hint: Expand right pointer to accumulate sum. Once sum >= target, contract left pointer continuously to record minimal length.
commonMistakes: Returning infinity when no valid subarray exists instead of 0
Using a static window size or nested loops resulting in O(n²)
followUpQuestions: How can you solve this in O(n log n) using Binary Search over Prefix Sums?
What if the array contains negative numbers?

questions.name: Find All Anagrams in a String
questions.description: Given two strings s and p, return an array of all the start indices of p's anagrams in s.
questions.interviewQuestion: How do you locate all occurrences of string anagram permutations within a larger text string?
questions.hint: Maintain a fixed-size sliding window of length `p.length` and compare frequency maps as the window slides.
commonMistakes: Rebuilding frequency counts from scratch for every window position
Not deleting or zeroing out character frequencies when left window edge moves forward
followUpQuestions: How can you track character matches in O(1) time without array comparisons?
How does this problem compare to Permutation in String?
